comparisons.peer_topic: Shareholder Returns and Stock Repurchase Program
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD returned $862 million to shareholders in 2024 through stock repurchases, with $4.7 billion remaining available under a program that has no termination date and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclosed their share repurchase activity and remaining authorization for fiscal year 2024 under a program with no termination date. NVIDIA repurchased 21 million shares for $9.7 billion with $22.5 billion remaining, following a $25.0 billion authorization increase in August 2023. In contrast, AMD repurchased 5.9 million shares for $862 million, leaving $4.7 billion remaining. While both programs allow for suspension or discontinuation, AMD explicitly stated its lack of obligation to acquire stock, whereas NVIDIA highlighted the specific recent authorization increase.

sentences.text: In August 2023, our Board of Directors approved an increase to our share repurchase program of an additional $25.0 billion, without expiration.
During fiscal year 2024, we repurchased 21 million shares of our common stock for $9.7 billion.
As of January 28, 2024, we were authorized, subject to certain specifications, to repurchase additional shares of our common stock up to $22.5 billion.
During the twelve months ended December 28, 2024, we returned a total of $862 million to shareholders through the repurchase of 5.9 million shares of common stock under our stock repurchase program.
As of December 28, 2024, $4.7 billion remained available for future stock repurchases under this program.
The stock repurchase program does not obligate us to acquire any common stock, has no termination date and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.
